title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working sketch of the cohomology of Eilenberg–MacLane objects for the additive group G_a over F_p, with coefficients in G_a. It belongs to the circle of ideas around Breen's work on Ext(G_a,G_a), which the next page continues with the vanishing of Ext^i(G_a^parf, G_a^parf) for i>1 on the perfect site.

(1) Steenrod operations with ring coefficients (top of page). For an F_p-algebra R one has H^*(X,R) = H^*(X,F_p) ⊗_{F_p} R. Steenrod operations extend as P^i_R = P^i ⊗ 1 for i>0 (degree 2i(p-1)). P^0_R, however, is P^0 ⊗ F, where F is the Frobenius of R. So in the 'coefficient ring' setting P^0 is no longer the identity but a Frobenius-semilinear operation.

(2) Setting. G_a is the structure sheaf on (Sch/F_p), with some topology. K(G_a,n) is the simplicial sheaf G_a ⊗ Λ^n ψ, i.e. the Dold–Kan image of G_a[n]. Following Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, around 3.2.1.18–19, p.69):
- Hypercohomology of a simplicial sheaf X is H^p(X,F) = Ext^p(Z(X),F) = colim over fibrant/quasi-isomorphic replacements X'→X of [X', K(F,p)].
- Natural cohomology operations Ext^p(Z(−),F) → Ext^q(Z(−),G) of type (F,p,G,q) are classified by H^q(K(F,p),G).
The reference to Epstein, 'Steenrod operations in homological algebra' (Invent. Math. 1, 1966) supplies Steenrod operations for cohomology of simplicial sheaves / topoi.

(3) Link with derived functors of Sym. Since the global functions on G_a ⊗ V form Sym(V^∨), one gets H^n(K(G_a,m),G_a) = R^n Sym(F_p[m]), the n-th derived functor in the Dold–Puppe sense. This is the dual of L_nΓ(F_p[m]), the derived functor of divided powers. Hence the page title 'Foncteurs dérivés de Sym'.

(4) Theorem. Let 𝒜 be the F_p-algebra generated by P^i (i≥0, deg 2i(p-1)) subject to the Adem relations but not P^0=1; this is the 'big' Steenrod algebra of Epstein/May type. Then H^*(K(G_a,m),G_a) is the free graded-commutative algebra on the admissible monomials of 𝒜 of excess < m, applied to the fundamental class. A variant for an arbitrary F_p-algebra R: H^*(K(R,m),R) is free graded-commutative over R, generated by the Hom(R,R)-module freely generated by admissible monomials, i.e. classes P^I f i_m with f ∈ Hom(R,R).

(5) Proof sketch. As classically (Cartan/Serre):
- compute H^*(K(G_a,1),G_a);
- induct on n using Borel's transgression theorem and the Leray–Serre spectral sequence of K(G_a,n-1) → * → K(G_a,n).
The ingredients for K(G_a,1) are:
- the bar picture G_a^3 ⇉ G_a^2 ⇉ G_a, with cochains polynomial algebras k[x,y,z] ← k[x,y] ← k[x];
- u_1 ∈ H^1 = Hom(G_a,G_a);
- a class β ∈ H^2(K(G_a,1),G_a) given by the Witt extension 0→G_a→W_2→G_a→0, the analogue of the Bockstein of 0→Z/p→Z/p^2→Z/p→0;
- Lazard's computation of the cohomology of the classical 'analyseur' (Lazard, 'Lois de groupes et analyseurs', Ann. ENS 1955), as an alternative route.

(6) Reduction to finite fields. Classes in H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a) represented by polynomial cochains of degree < p^n in each variable map injectively to H^*(K(F_{p^n},n),F_{p^n}). So the computation reduces to the known cohomology of K(F_q,1) with F_q coefficients. This is a 'generic cohomology'-type comparison between algebraic-group cohomology and finite-group cohomology.

Overall purpose: compute Ext^*(G_a,G_a) on the big (and then perfect) site. The next page does this via the universal coefficient spectral sequence Ext^i(H_j(K(G_a,n)),G_a) ⇒ H^{i+j}(K(G_a,n),G_a), which is exactly Breen's strategy.
errors: As stated, the theorem generates 𝒜 only by the P^i. For p odd the Bockstein-type class β (Witt extension), which the page itself introduces in H^2(K(G_a,1),G_a), must also be included among the generators (Epstein/May-type algebra with β), otherwise even the K(G_a,1) computation is wrong. For p=2 one should use Sq^i. This is probably a shorthand omission.

The admissibility/excess condition needs adapting when P^0 ≠ 1: P^0 acts as Frobenius, and monomials with P^0 are not trivially reducible. The excess bound must be read with the convention for the big Steenrod algebra; the page leaves this implicit.

The formula H^n(K(G_a,m),G_a) = R^n Sym(F_p[m]) is only correct on affine (cohomologically trivial) pieces, i.e. for the Zariski or presheaf-level computation. For finer topologies one needs that G_a has no higher cohomology on affines, which holds for fpqc/fppf/étale. So this is fine but tacit.
The injectivity claim into H^*(K(F_{p^n},n),F_{p^n}) for cochains of degree < p^n per variable is asserted without proof; the indices n/m are used inconsistently.

ideas.what: Steenrod operations with coefficients in an F_p-algebra R, where P^0 becomes Frobenius on R rather than the identity
ideas.modern_name: Big Steenrod algebra / algebraic Steenrod operations (Epstein, May 'A general algebraic approach to Steenrod operations')

ideas.what: Cohomology operations between sheaf hypercohomologies classified by H^q(K(F,p),G) in the derived category of simplicial sheaves
ideas.modern_name: Representability of operations by Eilenberg–MacLane objects in a topos

ideas.what: H^n(K(G_a,m),G_a) = R^n Sym(F_p[m]), dual to L_nΓ(F_p[m])
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe derived functors of Sym/Γ; functor cohomology

ideas.what: H^*(K(G_a,m),G_a) is free graded-commutative on admissible monomials of excess < m in a Steenrod algebra without P^0=1, plus the version for any F_p-algebra R
ideas.modern_name: Breen's computation of the cohomology of Eilenberg–MacLane objects of G_a
ideas.usually_credited_to: L. Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif', Publ. Math. IHES 48 (1978)

ideas.what: Witt-vector extension W_2 as Bockstein class β in H^2(K(G_a,1),G_a)
Comparison: polynomial cochains of degree < p^n per variable inject into cohomology of K(F_{p^n},n) with F_{p^n} coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Generic cohomology / comparison of rational and finite-group cohomology

missed.claim: This is a record of Grothendieck working through, or annotating, Breen's computation of H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a) and Ext(G_a,G_a) on the big and perfect sites. He explicitly frames it as 'derived functors of Sym' (dual of L Γ). The results themselves are Breen's and published; the novelty is only historical: Grothendieck's engagement with the topic around 1976, linked to the divided-power de Rham complex.
missed.quote: H^n(K(G_a,m),G_a) = R^n Sym(F_p[m]) = dual de L^nΓ (F_p[m])
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This identification anticipates the functor-cohomology viewpoint (strict polynomial functors, Friedlander–Suslin, FFSS) that later systematized Breen's computations. However, that connection is already known in the literature (FFSS cite Breen).

deep.surprise_reason: The content matches Breen's published work (Publ. IHES 1978 and the perfect-site Ext vanishing) together with standard Epstein/Illusie machinery. Seeing Grothendieck take these notes is of historical interest, but no new result or uncredited connection is evident.
transcription_corrections: 'Ranneau de car p≥0' should read 'Anneau de car p ≠ 0' (or 'p > 0').
'Ext^p(Λ(X),F) = lim_{X'→X fibrant}': the arrow is labelled 'qis' (quasi-isomorphism), with X' fibrant; Λ here is the free abelian functor Z(·).
'P^0_R = P^0_1 ⊗ F' is better read as 'P^0_R = P^0 ⊗ F' with F the Frobenius of R.
'2X →f K(A,q)' is likely 'ZX →f K(A,q)' (free abelian simplicial sheaf on X).
'H^*(K(R,m),R) = Alg anticomm libre /R eng par Hom(R,R)-module libre eng par les monomes admissibles, f ∈ Hom(R,R)', with classes ⊕ P^I f i_n.
'O. de op' is likely 'Alg. des op' (algebra of operations); '𝒪' denotes the structure sheaf G_a.
